lawyer:
Abdul Hameed Chowdhury with Shah Mushtak Ahmed and Shaikh Shamsul Alam, Advocates ----- For the Appellant 
AFM Shahid, DAG with MA Hafiz, AAG ----- For the State
parties:
Saheb Ali Miah ----- Appellant
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
This appeal under section 10 of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 at the instance of accused Md. Saheb Ali Miah, ex-member of Nagarkanda Union Parishad arises out of the Judgment and order dated 6.9.1990 passed by Mr. AFM Mostafa, Assistant Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Faridpur in Special Case No. 36 of 1990 convicting the aforesaid accused appellant under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, Act II of 1947 on admission of his guilt and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 years and to pay a fine of Taka 10,000.00, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for six months more. 

 3. The case being Nagarkanda PS Case No. 7 dated 31.8.86 was started on the basis of the FIR lodged with the said police station by one Md. Harunur-Rashid, Assistant Inspector, District Anti-Corruption Bureau, Faridpur, He himself took up the investigation of the case, seized some a1amats, examined witnesses under section 161 CrPC and wrote to the Government for proper sanction for prosecution for the accused being a public servant and waited for the same before filing the charge-sheet. A number of reminders were sent to the Investagating Officer by the Court of the Upazila Magistrate for the Police report in the case but the Investigating Officer, the said Harunur Rashid, informed the court of the Magistrate by his Memo dated 8.8.88 that the investigation was already completed but the same could not be submitted for want of the sanction order and the same was communicated to the court of the learned Magistrate vide Memo of the Anti-Corruption Bureau dated 26.11.86. The accused also remained in ascendance since the beginning of the case in spite of is nuance of Warrant of Arrest and Proclamation and ultimately he was arrested by the Police and produced before the Upazila Magistrate on 14.6.90 and thereafter he prayed for bail but his prayer for bail was rejected. Meanwhile, the Investigating Officer came to know that the accused Saheb Ali Miah ceased to be a member of the Union Council as well as the Chairman of the project committee, that means he ceased to be a public servant and in such circumstances there being no necessity for sanction, the Investigating Officer submitted the charge-sheet on 7.2.90 showing that the accused was still in ascendance. Of course he was subsequently arrested on 14.6.90 as stated above. Thereafter, the case-record was transmitted to the court of the learned Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Faridpur who took cognizance of the offences and the case was accordingly numbered as Special Case No. 36 of 1990 under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. Before arrival of the records of the case to the court of the learned Special Judge, the accused however was able to obtain his bail from the court of the learned Upazila Magistrate and on 10.7.1990 when the case record was received by the learned Special Judge he appeared before the court and on his prayer he was granted fresh basil by the learned Special Judge. The learned Sessions Judge-in-charge and Special Judge fixed 21.8.90 for accusation and also for evidence and accordingly passed order for issuance of summons upon the prosecution witness No. 1. On 21.8.90 he recorded the attendance of one PW and thereafter transferred the case to the court of the Assistant Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Faridpur for disposal, which accordingly received the case-record on 21.8.90 and recorded the hazira of the accused who was already on bail and also one witness for the prosecution. The accused filed an application for adjournment which was allowed and 6.9.90 was fixed for evidence and accordingly, direction was given to issue summons upon the witnesses. On 6.9.90, five witnesses for the prosecution filed hazira. The accused Saheb Ali also filed hazira in Court. The learned Special Judge on hearing the learned Advocate for the parties and on examination of the case record framed accusation (charge) against the accused appellant to the effect that he being a member of the Nagarkanda Union Parishad was appointed Chairman of the Project Committee for reconstruction of the road from Nagarkanda Chandhat upto the house of Kabir Miah of village Kodalia under the Nibir Polly Purta Works Programme for the year 1985-86 and as the Project Chairman he withdrew by 3 cheques from 18.3.86 to 17.5.86 a total sum of Taka 45,000.00 and spent out of the same a sum of Taka 37,868.59 only for the work of the said project and did not utilisc the rest sum of Taka 71,31.41 and in spite of reminders he did not return and deposit the said amount of Taka 7,131.41 in the Government account and thus being a public servant by misusing of power he misappropriated the said amount of Taka 7,131.41, and thereby committed an offence under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. According to the prosecution, the said accusation (charge) was read out and explained in Bengali to the accused Saheb Ali Miah who pleaded guilty and prayed for mercy. The learned Special Judge on such admission of guilty convicted the accused appellant under section 409 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II, 1947 and taking a soft view for such admission and prayer' for mercy he convicted and sentenced him as stated above by the impugned judgment and order dated 6.9:90. The accused being aggrieved by the said order of conviction and sentence preferred the present appeal in this court. 

 5. Mr. Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellant, took me through the FIR, the charge-sheet, the accusations and the order-sheet of the case and also the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence and thereafter assailed the same on various grounds though passed on admission of guilt. His first contention is, that the accused appellant was a public servant but no sanction was obtained from the Government for his prosecution and hence for violation of the provisions of section 6(5) of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 1958, the whole trial was vitiated and the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence were bad and illegal. 

 6. In reply to the above submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant, Mr. AFM Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, submitted that at the time of the alleged occurrence the accused being a member of the Union Council and also the Chairman of the Project Committee, was a public servant and even during the period for investigation of the case he continued to be a public servant and before submission of the charge-sheet against him, sanction from the Govt. was sought for by the Investigating Officer, but meanwhile the term of the accused as Chairman, Project Committee and member of the Union Council expired and he ceased to be a public servant and the Investigating Officer therefore without any sanction order from the Government, submitted the charge-sheet on 7.2.90 and thereafter the case- records, were sent to the learned Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Faridpur for necessary action and the learned Special Judge took cognizance of the case on receipt of the records on 10.7.90. Thus at the time of taking cognizance, the accused appellant was not a public servant and therefore there was no necessity of any sanction from the government for the prosecution of this appellant and hence there was no violation of any provisions of section 6(5) of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 and as such no illegality in the trial of the accused appellant for want of sanction as alleged by the learned Advocate for the appellant. In support of his contention, the learned Deputy Attorney-General however referred to a decision in the case of Jamdhar Khan Vs. State, reported in 27 DLR (AD) 35 which laid down that no sanction would be necessary when the accused ceased to be a public servant. I therefore accept the contention of the learned DAG and find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant on the above point. 

 7. The learned advocate for the appellant thereafter contended that the trial of the accused appellant was illegal and unauthorised as the charge-sheet in this case was not submitted within the statutory period as fixed under section 167(5A) CrPC which was made applicable by amendment of the Criminal Law Amendment Act 1958 and the time for filing charge-sheet was also extended therein. According to the learned Advocate for the appellant, the prosecution was entitled to get 280 + 30 that is, in all 310 days from the date of lodging the FIR till the filing of the charge-sheet and the said period in this case expired on 30.3.87 but the charge-sheet here as already stated was filed on 7.2.90 after quite a long time which was illegal and unauthorised. The learned DAG as against the above submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant submitted by drawing my attention to the order sheet of the court of the learned Magistrate that from the very beginning of the case, even after submission of the charge-sheet, the accused remained in ascendance and ultimately he was arrested by the Police on 14.6.90 and produced before the Court for trial. Further, it is on the record that Government has written for sanction for the prosecution of the accused being a public servant at the time of lodging the FIR and in the process some delay was caused waiting for the sanction order but ultimately before submission of the charge-sheet the accused-appellant ceased to be the member of the Union Parishad and Chairman of the Project Committee, as such public servant and thereafter without waiting for any order of sanction, the charge-sheet was submitted on 7.2.90 and thus some substantial period was spent up in the process but in view of the proviso to section 167(5) CrPC the period so spent awaiting sanction of the Govt, for the prosecution of the accused appellant should be added to the statutory period for submission of the charge-sheet and if added it would be found that the charge-sheet was submitted well within time and there was no illegality or irregularity in the submission of the charge-sheet or in the trial as alleged. 

 11.  13. Mr. Chowdhury, the learned advocate for the appellant, on the other hand, submitted that section 412 CrPC has no manner of application to the instant case; firstly, for the reason that the present appeal was not filed under section 412 of the CrPC but under section 10 of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 and secondly, the answer to the accusation (charge) shows that there was no admission or pleading of guilt by the accused-appellant himself in his own words. The answer to the query of the court appears to have been noted in the words of the learned Judge in violation of the provisions of section 243 CrPC. It is further contended by Mr. Chowdhury that even if section 412 CrPC is a bar against raising any question with regard to the validity or propriety of the conviction of the accused and the section confines itself only to the extent and legality of the sentence, still this court has ample power under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to treat this petition of appeal as a revisional application and examine the propriety or legality of the conviction as well as the sentence passed against the appellant. 

 14: Now, for proper consideration and appreciation of the above submissions of the learned Advocates from both the sides as to the above points, first of all I would like to refer to sub-section 3 of section 6 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 which runs as follows: 

 15. Chapter XX of the said Code relates to trials of summons cases by Magistrate, but this chapter of the said Code has been made applicable to the trial of cases under the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1958 as mentioned above and this Act provides in section 6, the procedure for the trial of cases and powers of Special Judge, Additional Sessions Judge, Assistant Sessions Judge, a Metropolitan Magistrate, or Magistrate, 1st Class who may be appointed and deemed to be Special Judges for trial of the offences under this Act. Now, Chapter XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure starts from section 241. But section 241A of the said Code has been added by an amendment which speaks of discharge of an accused in some cases when the charge is found to be groundless and section 242 of the said Code speaks of framing the charges of accusation and it is as follows:
